subject: Serving change coordination — SLA opt-outs, fallthrough mapping, comms handoff
messages:
From: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Samira Khan <samira@acme.com>, Acme Platform Team <acme-platform@acme.com>
Date: Sun, 21 Nov 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Serving change coordination — SLA opt-outs, fallthrough mapping, comms handoff

Team / Acme,

Quick sync: Acme is aiming to cut over from model-v1 to model-v2 on 2027-12-06 (customer request). They want a short canary followed by full traffic the next week. Before we sign off I need three cross-functional confirmations so we can freeze the comms and legal asks: 

1) SLA opt-out window: Acme has asked if they can be on a temporary SLA exception (lowered availability SLA) for a limited period during the cutover (they offered a 45-day exception window). We need: a) product sign-off on guardrails that will be enforced during opt-out and b) PS/CS plan to communicate risk.

2) Fallthrough mapping / model compatibility: Marissa — can you confirm the deterministic fallback mapping between v2 and v1 for the endpoints they use (text-gen, chat-stream). We need an explicit mapping and a list of behavioral regressions we expect so Sales/CS can prepare messaging. See attached compatibility_matrix.xlsx for my initial notes.

3) Canary + comms cadence: Laura / Karthik — can you confirm a canary window (proposed 48 hours, extended if we see >0.5% user-facing regressions), monitoring hooks (SLOs to watch), and who will own the external comms and in-product banners? See canary_rollout_plan.pdf attached. 

Acme (Samira) — if you'd prefer a longer canary or different rollback criteria, say so now; we can propose an alternative plan but we need to finalize by EOD Monday so Legal can prepare the exception language.

Action items I want by EOD Mon:
- Marissa: fallback mapping + short risk bullet list (one-paragraph)
- Laura: comms owner and banner text draft
- Karthik: canary SLOs and acceptance criteria
- Connor: I will draft the exception language and loop Legal once you confirm scopes

Thanks — keeping this tight to avoid back-and-forth with Acme next week.

Connor O'Brien
Director, Product Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachments: compatibility_matrix.xlsx (spreadsheet), canary_rollout_plan.pdf (pdf)
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Samira Khan <samira@acme.com>
Date: Sun, 21 Nov 2027 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Serving change coordination — SLA opt-outs, fallthrough mapping, comms handoff

Connor —

Thanks, copying quick answers inline.

• Comms owner: I can take the external comms and the in-product banner. I will draft a short banner that reads: "Planned model upgrade in progress — you may see slight differences in output quality. Contact your CSM for details." Will share the banner text and the MD file by Monday morning.

• Banner timing / cadence: proposed: banner up during canary + 24 hours after full traffic flip. If we see regressions in canary we leave banner up and apply a holding pattern.

• External notification: one email the morning of the full flip (only for impacted API keys) + an in-console banner. For customers needing more detail we’ll add a one-pager.

One ask: Legal will need the exact duration and acceptance criteria to prepare the exception. Connor — please confirm whether we accept Acme's 45-day opt-out or we want a shorter (30-day) exception window.

Laura Bennett
Head of Product Marketing
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Serving change coordination — SLA opt-outs, fallthrough mapping, comms handoff

Connor / all —

High-level fallback summary (short):
- Endpoint: /v1/generate -> primary: model-v2; fallback: model-v1 (same API contract).
- Chat endpoint: /v1/chat/stream -> primary: chat-v2; fallback: chat-v1.

Behavioral regressions likely during fallback: shorter completions in ~1.2% of calls (token budget differences), slight prompt-interpretation variance on multi-turn flows (~0.6%), and potential latency increase when falling back to v1 for autopopulated sessions (because v1 is hosted in a different pool).

Mitigations: prefix/KV cache warming during canary, keep canary traffic targeted to non-critical org IDs, and a hard fallback throttle (do not auto-fallback more than 5% of requests per org per hour).

I attached a compact mapping summary to compatibility_matrix.xlsx (tab: mappings). If we need a more conservative plan we can keep Acme on v1 for a longer staged rollout.

Quick ask for Connor: if Legal insists on timeboxed exceptions, we should include the above mitigation limits as mandatory conditions in the exception. Otherwise we risk noisy regressions.

Marissa Cole
Staff Software Engineer, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Serving change coordination — SLA opt-outs, fallthrough mapping, comms handoff

Connor / Redwood team —

Thanks for the clear breakdown and for looping us in. Acme is OK with a 48-hour canary but would prefer the 45-day opt-out window as a safeguard for our larger enterprise tenants; our procurement and legal teams requested that specifically. We are open to the mitigation limits Marissa suggested (please make them mandatory in the exception language).

Also can we request that the canary include a small percentage (~10%) of traffic from our highest-value customer orgs so we can validate revenue-critical flows? If that looks risky to Redwood we can reduce to 5% and run an extended canary.

Please confirm: if we accept a shorter opt-out (30 days) today, will Redwood provide an SLA credit or an escalation channel as compensation? We want to understand the trade-offs.

Samira Khan
Head of Platform Engineering
Acme Corp
